bayts.text: I have been enriched by Allah together with the Prophet, and He, through him, is for me with what is well-pleasing.
I have won preservation from impurities in this abode and in that (of the Hereafter).
Through Allah I have sought, through the Prophet, purity, safety, glad tidings and pardon.
O Appreciative (Ash-Shakūr), be for me, by Your noble Face, with glad tidings and ease that never cease.
By Your noble Face, purify my years of all turbidity, O Lord of creatures and of the Command.
Join to the striving of the first forerunners (Qurʾān 9:100) my striving, and give glad tidings of me to all the most perfect.
Accept my gratitude, O Appreciative, and protect me until the Gardens, with aspirations and safety.
I have repented to You today: so accept the repentance, and grant me, by the right of Your Face, the Book.
Favour me forever with purity, and through health make me free of need for healing.
Lead to me the sciences of the pure elect, like (those) of the saints and the learned, and make my attainment great for me.
To You (I address) today my discourse, with intercession, through the Chosen, the Elect, light of the messengers.
Increase me in knowledge, by the sanctity of the Prophet, and turn no injustice toward my sides.
Teach me, O God, a knowledge never seen for any other than me, and for any other than me it shall not be seen.
Lead to me the unveiling of the saints, and lead to me the knowledge of the others (the learned), and be lavish to me with success.
Grant me by grace felicity, by the right of Your Face, and the wonder that breaks the customary course.
Favour me with the glad tidings of time, until the Gardens, and be for me with safety.
Accept my gifts for the Prophet, out of generosity, O best of those who have enriched and of those who have been generous.
Gladden the Messenger of Allah with the letters of it (this poem), and be lavish to me forever with good.
Lead to the Messenger of Allah, adornment of mankind, from me, glad tidings beyond counting.
Muḥammad — may Allah bless him — his loftiness has become clear to every (being) endowed with reason.
That Abū l-Qāsim (Muḥammad) is the light of the prophets has become clear to all but the wretched dullards.
The Book of Aḥmad has abrogated every other, and truly it shall not be abrogated by any other.
Our Prophet: his Book has completed what (came) before it, and has adorned every other.
The peace of Him Who is exalted above consort and child (Qurʾān 72:3) upon the son of ʿAbd Allāh, the most excellent of offspring.
He to Whom none is equal (Qurʾān 112:4) has sent Muḥammad, and has already spared (us) whoever denied.
O Splitter (Al-Fāliq, Qurʾān 6:95), bless forever and grant peace to him whose precedence is known.
O Benefactor (An-Nāfiʿ), bless with a peace that has no end him who is the beginning of the noble and (their) seal.
